title: Luda
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Shabbat 96b they said: “But Luda taught.” Yuchasin writes that he lived in Shmuel’s time. Hyman takes this to refer to Shabbat 137a: Shmuel says that an infant whose fever has left him is given seven full days to recover. The anonymous discussion asks, “Do we require complete twenty-four-hour periods?” and answers, “Come and hear, for Luda taught.” Hyman argues that there is no proof at all from this, since the citation belongs to the anonymous Gemara.

notes.text: Luda’s baraita is cited by the anonymous discussion following Shmuel’s statement. Hyman argues that this does not prove that Luda was Shmuel’s contemporary. The 96b numeral is retained.
Shabbat 137a gives Shmuel’s fever-recovery rule, followed by an anonymous question and Luda’s baraita. This sequence does not itself establish a direct encounter or contemporaneity.
